Crude oil futures settle at $83.27 The US government deficit in July was the highest in any month since 2021 Canadian consumers continued spending through another challenging quarter -- RBC data US treasury sells 10 year notes at a high yield of 4.683% WARNING: There is a long way to go until the next Fed Meeting European stocks close lower as traders head for the exits Cleveland Fed median CPI +0.3% vs +0.2% prior EIA weekly US crude oil inventories +17.423K vs -1405K expected Gold tests the weekly high as the CPI report cools the rate hike talk Canada Building Permits for June 18.5% vs 0.8% estimate US July CPI 3.4% y/y vs 3.4% expected Kickstart video for August 12: US Dollar is lower ahead of key CPI report investingLive European markets wrap: Gold stays poised, dollar tentative awaiting US CPI report The main catalyst for markets today was the July U.S. CPI report, which came in largely as expected while showing some further moderation in annual inflation.

Headline CPI rose 0.1% month over month and 3.4% year over year, both matching expectations, with the annual rate easing from 3.5% in June.

Core CPI increased 0.2% for the month and 2.5% year over year, also matching forecasts, with the annual core rate falling from 2.6% to its lowest level since February.

Shelter costs remained firm, with both owners' equivalent rent and primary rents rising 0.3%, while medical care and airfares also increased.

On the softer side, energy prices fell 1.5% and gasoline dropped 2.9%, helping restrain headline inflation.

Overall, the report gave the Fed additional room to remain on hold in September, with the market-implied probability of a September rate hike slipping to around 39% from 44% before the release.

However, there is still another round of inflation and employment data ahead of the September FOMC meeting, leaving plenty of time for the outlook to change.
